checklist_items.1.1: The create dialog shows name and scope with no hidden form item. Name is a required textbox, empty by default, with no unit or control range. Scope has two radios with all model services checked; no deployment combobox is present in the default state. Reading the form sends no key write. POST /api/v1/apikeys sends name, all_deployments=true and deployment_ids=[]. The 201 response carries the name. After reload the row shows name and prefix; the independent GET keeps name, prefix, created_at, all_deployments=true and deployments=[]. Choosing a deployment subset is not exercised here.

partial.12.7: The confirmation carries the name and the consequence and both are asserted: the current product locale's revoke.confirm string with {{name}} replaced must be visible inside the viewport. With open access off, it explains that revoking the last active token leaves /v1 refusing every request until another token is created, unless an administrator explicitly turns on keyless access in Settings > Security. Cancelling it is required to send no mutation and to leave the token still authenticating /v1/models. What keeps this binding below the strongest form is a contract difference rather than an absent assertion: this resource is revoked, not deleted. DELETE /api/v1/apikeys/{prefix} answers {'status': 'revoked'} and the row stays listed carrying revoked_at, which the product's own test pins down as TestAPIKeyRevokeKeepsTheKeyListed (internal/server/api/apikey_validation_test.go:85), including a second revoke answering 200 with revoked_at unmoved at :121-125 - a delete is not idempotent that way. The case asserts the same shape from the outside: the active set is filtered by revoked_at, the revoked token appears in revoked rather than active, and it stops authenticating. So the name/impact and the failed-path halves of a delete confirmation have no object here: there is no destructive removal of the record, no in-use reference that could block a revoke, and therefore no half-applied-change half to prove. Recorded as the resource's own contract rather than as untested ground.

checklist_items.7.1: The create dialog has a name textbox and a scope radio group; neither is an entered credential, so masked/reveal controls have nothing to act on here - the key is generated by the server and shown once after creation, which is 7.3. The fields are inventoried before typing: one textbox with the name label, empty value, declared placeholder, aria-required, no maxlength, no unit or number input; two scope radios with all checked, no combobox or switch in the default state; exactly two form items and none hidden. Reading it is asserted to send no key write. Then the empty string and a whitespace-only value are each submitted and required to show the product's nameRequired message on the dialog, to mark the field aria-invalid, and to leave the mutation record empty. Proven by mutation: dropping whitespace:true from the name rule in APIKeysPage makes the case fail on the aria-invalid attribute for the whitespace value.
checklist_items.7.2: N/A: this component has no edit operation. The management API exposes only GET, POST and DELETE for these credentials, and the card offers create and revoke only, so there is no edit form whose blank field could mean either keep or clear. Replacing a credential means creating a new one and revoking the old, which is what the case already does.
checklist_items.7.5: The three credential planes are kept apart by shape and by what each one authorises, and both halves are asserted. The inference key is required to be a 51-character value starting with gw-, so it cannot be mistaken for a platform token, and the platform token is separately required to start with gwp_. The behaviour split is asserted with real requests rather than by reading a field: the inference key is accepted as a Bearer credential on /v1/models and refused with 401 once a character is appended, while the same key against the management route /api/v1/nodes is refused with 401 and AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED - so an inference key never stands in for a management session. The expiry side is not invented: inference keys expose no expiry control at all, which the field inventory asserts, and the platform token's own lifetime is asserted by its own case, so no expiry widget is claimed where the product has none.
checklist_items.7.6: No credential value the component holds is exposed by a read, an error or an artifact. The independent GET is required to return an exact field set - name, prefix, created_at, all_deployments and deployments - with the prefix being the first twelve characters, so the stored form is a hash and a prefix and the full secret is never recoverable from it. The DOM is asserted to contain no occurrence of the secret and so is the whole persisted collection, and the row is required to show only the prefix. The error plane is asserted too: a tampered secret sharing a valid prefix is refused with 401 and the product's fixed invalid-key body, which is a constant message rather than an echo of anything sent. The server log is written out through the artifact redactor and the artifacts are scanned, with a scan failure failing the run, so a secret reaching a log or a download rejects the artifacts rather than shipping them. Proven by mutation: storing the full token as the prefix in CreatePlatformToken makes the case fail on the token prefix.
